sections.h2: Where to submit a Lucas County deed
sections.html:
The Lucas County Recorder works from One Government Center, Suite 700, in downtown Toledo, OH 43604. Call 419-213-4400 for the counter or write to Recorder@co.lucas.oh.us. Weekday hours are 8 AM to 4:30 PM, and electronic recording stops at 4 PM.

You can walk a deed in, mail it, or e-record through a partner company. The office strongly encourages electronic recording or mailing, and it names CSC, ePN and Simplifile as the e-recording partners. If you mail a deed, include a self addressed stamped envelope or add return postage to the payment. The office accepts cash or a check payable to the Lucas County Recorder.

Return postage for a standard one ounce first class letter is $1.00. Add that amount whenever you do not enclose a stamped envelope, since a payment that comes up short can slow intake.

The basic fee is $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage and $8.00 for every extra page. The $5.00 increase behind that figure came from Senate Bill 94, and the schedule lists $39.00 as a minimum.

A master mortgage reference carries no reference fee. Plats are priced by size, at ten cents per square inch with a $40.00 minimum per page.

sections.h2: What the Auditor charges before recording
sections.html:
Lucas County's Auditor publishes a real estate transfers fact sheet with two charges. The transfer fee is $0.50 per parcel. The conveyance fee is $4.00 for every $1,000 of the sale price, and some transfers outlined in law are exempt from it.

Transfers caused by a death, adding survivorship, or placing the property into your own trust are generally exempt and cost only the $0.50 per parcel. The Auditor cannot prepare a deed, and an attorney is the safer choice because a wrong detail can get the document rejected or cause trouble years later. The Auditor's main line is 419-213-4406.

The statewide rules behind these steps are in section 319.202, which requires the buyer's value statement before the Auditor endorses a deed, and section 319.54, which lists the exempt transfers.

Recorded documents after 1985 can be viewed through the Recorder's Online Recordings tool, which is run by a document technology vendor. The Auditor's AREIS property system shows deeds and transfers as public records.

AREIS shows how title is held, which helps when you are sorting out a sale after a death:

  • Property held in survivorship carries the code ORSURVTC after the owners' names.
  • Property held by a trustee shows the word Trustee after the name.
  • A transfer on death confirmation appears as document type OD on the Transfers page.

For records from before 1985, call the counter on 419-213-4400 and ask how to request a copy.

Residents get solicitations from document retrieval companies that quote $49.50 to $87.00 for a certified copy of a deed. The county sells the same copy for far less. Copies of all land records are available from the office, often for as little as $2.00.

The fee schedule backs that up: assisted copies are $2.00 per page and a certification is $1.00 per document. If you have an escrow account with the office, a copy order form can be emailed to the Recorder or faxed to 419-213-4284. Copies are paid by cash, check or escrow account only.

Toledo is the county seat and largest city. The other cities are Maumee, Oregon, Sylvania and Waterville, and the villages include Holland, Ottawa Hills, Whitehouse and Swanton. The county had 423,347 residents in July 2025 and 201,974 housing units. The median owner-occupied value is $163,900, owner occupancy is 62.0 percent and median gross rent is $934. With nearly four homes in ten rented, many Lucas County sales involve a tenant-occupied house.

Beyond deeds, the office accepts a full range of paperwork for the permanent land record:

  • Certificates of transfer, deeds and land contracts.
  • Mortgages, liens and real estate financing statements.
  • Plats and powers of attorney.
  • Military service discharges, and any other document made recordable by the Revised Code.

For lien paperwork the schedule gives $5.00 for a federal tax lien, $3.00 for its release and $4.00 for a personal tax release. Bureau of Workers' Compensation liens and releases carry no fee. The e-recording partners also list direct lines: CSC at 866-652-0111, ePN at 888-325-3365 extension 11234, and Simplifile at 800-460-5657 extension 1031.

sections.h2: How the recording fee got to $39.00
sections.html: The state budget raised the fee for most documents by $6.00, to $34.00 for the first two pages, with half of all recording fees going to the Ohio Housing Trust Fund. A later $5.00 increase from Senate Bill 94 brought the figure to $39.00, under section 317.32. Counting a mailed deed's return postage in the payment avoids a delay at intake.

A title company orders the ownership search for a sale. The Recorder's online system covers documents recorded after 1985, so ask the title company how it will pull anything older.

Steps for a typical sale

The title company or an attorney drafts the deed, and you sign it. It goes to the Auditor for the value statement and the transfer and conveyance fees, then to the Recorder with the recording fee. If a lender is paid off, its release is recorded separately and each reference to the old mortgage adds the $4.00 notation charge. A cash sale skips the lender release, so there is one less filing to track. Before you head downtown, confirm the page count of the deed, because the fee is tied to it, and check that nothing on the document breaks the layout rules that bring the $20.00 charge.

faqs.q: How much is the basic recording fee in Lucas County?
faqs.a: The schedule lists $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage, with $8.00 for each additional page. A document that breaks the state layout rules draws a $20.00 non-compliance fee, and each reference for a marginal notation costs $4.00.

faqs.q: What are the Lucas County transfer and conveyance fees?
faqs.a: The Auditor's fact sheet shows $0.50 per parcel as the transfer fee and $4.00 for every $1,000 of the sale price as the conveyance fee. Transfers due to death, survivorship or moving the property into your own trust are generally exempt from the conveyance fee.

faqs.q: Does the Lucas County Recorder accept mailed deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder encourages mailing and e-recording. Include a self addressed stamped envelope or add return postage to the payment, and make the check payable to the Lucas County Recorder.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a military discharge in Lucas County?
faqs.a: No. The fee schedule lists no fee to record a DD-214 or to get certified copies of it from the Recorder.

faqs.q: Can the Lucas County Auditor prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The Auditor cannot prepare transfer documents, including deeds, and recommends hiring an attorney. Staff can answer questions about the transfer process at 419-213-4406.
